input.quote: 14.2.2 At-Will Termination by PB. PB may terminate this Agreement at any time after SFJ has paid or incurred a total of $60 million of Development Costs and prior to the date of receipt of the first Regulatory Approval upon [***] prior written notice to SFJ.
input.rationale: Article 14 gives PB an at-will right (14.2.2) but gates it twice: it is unavailable until SFJ has paid or incurred $60 million of Development Costs and closes once the first Regulatory Approval is received, so for the early (and the late) years of this multi-year program PB has no convenience exit at all — the playbook treats absence of a customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months as a deviation. Conversely, SFJ holds a near-convenience right in 14.2.10: it may terminate "in its sole discretion" and on immediate notice simply because it continues to disagree with a decision PB is contractually entitled to make, and PB then owes Development Costs plus 25% interest. That is below the fallback floor of a provider convenience right only at end of term on 90 days' notice, and it sits in walk-away territory. Redline therefore ungates 14.2.2 at 30 days' notice and deletes 14.2.10 with its payment consequence. Noted but not separately flagged: the 300% Development Cost exit payment in 14.2.2 exceeds the playbook's early-termination fee cap, but it is the priced return in this funding bargain (SFJ's other exits are cause- or event-based, e.g. Material Adverse Event, bankruptcy, Adverse Patent Impact, Program Transfer on PB default), so we accept it rather than press the preferred no-penalty position.

proposal.summary: Ungate PB's at-will termination right (30 days' notice, no $60M spend threshold) and delete SFJ's sole-discretion termination on JSC disagreement.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We need a real exit right, so we have removed the $60 million spend threshold and the pre-first-approval window from Section 14.2.2 and fixed notice at thirty (30) days; as drafted we would be locked in for the early years of a multi-year program. We have also deleted Section 14.2.10, which lets SFJ walk away in its sole discretion on immediate notice merely because it disagrees with a decision PB is entitled to make (and charges us Development Costs plus 25% interest for doing so); our playbook does not accept a provider convenience right on less than 90 days' notice. We accept the 300% exit payment in Section 14.2.2 as part of the funding economics.

ops.oldText: PB may terminate this Agreement at any time after SFJ has paid or incurred a total of $60 million of Development Costs and prior to the date of receipt of the first Regulatory Approval upon [***] prior written notice to SFJ.
ops.newText: PB may terminate this Agreement at any time upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to SFJ.
